title: Embedding ingress scheduler and capacity simulator for throughput planning
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Embeddings endpoint bursts cause either degraded p99 latency or over-provisioning. Current autoscaler reacts to GPU utilization and queue length but lacks an accurate model of ingress shaping, tenant burst reservations, and the latency cost of micro-batching. This ticket builds two complementary pieces: (1) an ingress scheduler that enforces SLO-aware micro-batching and priority-aware rate fences; and (2) a capacity simulator that replays historical traffic and 'what-if' scenarios to produce autoscaler configurations and recommended headroom budgets. Goals: reduce token-level unit cost for typical mixed workloads, keep p99 latency within SLO across tenants, and provide reliable forecasts for Dedicated capacity planning.
background: We observe frequent short bursts from conversational clients (many small payloads) and large batch embedding jobs. Naive batching either increases tail latency for low-latency tenants or wastes GPU cycles. Previous tickets focused on queue gating and warm pools; this work focuses on shaping at the ingress boundary with tenant-aware priorities and an offline simulator that teams can use to size reserved pools and soft quotas.
approach: Ingress scheduler: implement a pluggable scheduler component in the embedding router that does dynamic micro-batching based on measured inter-arrival times and per-tenant latency budgets. Core features: - SLA-driven batching window (max latency budget per request) - Priority token buckets with burst reservation (per-tenant short-term bursts) - Prefix-aware KV-cache hints to warm model cache for likely repeated embeddings - Backpressure signals to upstream SDKs when queues exceed soft headroom - Adaptive batch size caps that vary by model and sequence-length distribution Capacity simulator: a separate service that consumes historical request traces and simulates the scheduler+runtime to estimate p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU token throughput, and required slot counts under different policies. Support scenarios: traffic growth, tenant onboarding, large nightly batch jobs. Simulator output feeds the autoscaler tuning UI in Console.
design_decisions: 1) Scheduler should be colocated with existing embedding router for low-latency decision making; avoids extra network hop. 2) Use conservative default headroom of 20% for Dedicated pools, but let simulator recommend tuned headroom per customer. 3) Prioritize latency-sensitive tenants via short token-bucket windows rather than strict hard rate limits to preserve burstiness. 4) Simulator will use anonymized traces and configurable noise models to preserve privacy and cover unseen spikes.
tradeoffs: - Latency vs cost: tighter batching increases throughput and reduces cost but risks p99 latency regressions for low-latency clients. We default to SLO-first for production tenants and cost-first for low-priority 'bulk' tenants. - Complexity vs observability: introducing scheduler and simulator increases system complexity; added observability hooks and deterministic simulation traces are required for debugging. - Fairness vs utilization: burst reservations improve UX for paying customers but reduce pooled utilization; simulator will quantify utilization loss.
implementation_plan: M1 (2 weeks): Scheduler MVP with static SLA windows, simple priority buckets, and basic backpressure. Instrument detailed metrics: queue depth by tenant, batching size distribution, per-batch latency. M2 (2 weeks): Integrate KV-cache hints and adaptive batch caps; add end-to-end e2e tests and chaos tests for spikes. M3 (2 weeks): Capacity simulator alpha, replay historical data, export recommended headroom and slot counts. M4 (1 week): Console integration - show simulator outputs and suggested autoscale config; rollout to a small set of Dedicated customers. Rollout plan: feature-flagged; enable default for internal staging tenants; invite 3 pilot customers; monitor errors/latency for 2 weeks before wider rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler MVP deployed behind feature flag
p99 latency for low-latency tenants does not regress by more than 5% compared to baseline under pilot traffic
Unit cost (tokens/GPU-hour) for mixed workloads shows >=8% improvement in simulator-projected steady-state scenarios
Simulator reproduces historical peak within 10% accuracy for token throughput and p95 latency
Console shows recommended headroom and slot counts for at least 2 pilot customers
metrics_to_track: batch size distribution and percent of micro-batched requests
queue depth and average wait time
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Scheduler mis-configuration causes spike in p99 - Mitigation: start with conservative SLO windows, enable canary rollout, and automatic rollback on p99 breach
Risk: Simulator privacy concerns - Mitigation: anonymize request payloads, keep traces internal and allow opt-out for customer-specific replays
Risk: Interactions with existing autoscaler - Mitigation: expose simulator recommendations as advisory only; do not auto-commit changes until human review
testing_plan: - Unit tests for scheduler logic and priority buckets - Integration tests that replay synthetic mixed traffic with verifier measuring latency targets - Load tests (k6) with historical traces to validate simulator accuracy - Chaos experiments: sudden 10x spike and GPU OOM scenarios - Pilot deployment with 3 customers and realtime dashboards for 14 days
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike analysis completed; identified that 62% of embedding requests are under 128 tokens and highly bursty.
2026-02-20: Scheduler MVP prototype passed unit tests; integrated simple priority buckets; ready for staging smoke tests.
2026-02-28: Simulator ingested 7 days of anonymized traces and produced initial headroom recommendations; projection error for p95 is ~12% (working to improve).
2026-03-10: Pilot customer onboarding confirmed; feature flag gating and rollback hooks added. Observability dashboard for queue depth and batch sizing live in staging.
next_steps: 1) Finish PR review and land scheduler MVP in staging. 2) Improve simulator noise model to reduce p95 projection error under tail scenarios. 3) Run pilot for 14 days and collect cost/latency signals; iterate on headroom defaults.
estimated_cost_savings: Projected 8-15% token-level cost reduction for mixed workloads after tuning; savings vary by tenant mix and booking of burst reservations.
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the priority bucket parameters (burst window and sustained rate). We will tune these per-customer based on simulator output; recommend conservative defaults for initial rollout. Also review the proposed KV-cache hint API for privacy implications.
